40020088.author: पदार्थः
40020088.content: नारायणगिरिं towards the mountain Narayana, ते those, तु indeed, गर्जन्तः roaring, राक्षसाम्बुदाः the demon-clouds, ववर्षुः showered, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, वर्षेण with rain, इव like, अद्रिम् upon a mountain, अम्बुदाः clouds,

40020088.author: Translation
40020088.content: Those roaring demon-clouds, like actual clouds showering rain upon a mountain, indeed showered a rain of arrows upon the mountain-like Narayana (Vishnu/Rama).

40020089.author: पदार्थः
40020089.content: श्यामावदातः dark-complexioned and radiant, तैः by them, विष्णुः Vishnu, नीलैः by the blue ones, नक्तञ्चरोत्तमैः by the best of night-wanderers, वृतः surrounded, अञ्जनगिरीवासीत् became like a mountain of collyrium, वर्षमाणैः showering, पयोधरैः by clouds,

40020089.author: Translation
40020089.content: The dark-complexioned and radiant Vishnu, surrounded by those blue, best of night-wanderers, became like a collyrium mountain being showered upon by clouds.

40020090.author: पदार्थः
40020090.content: शलभाः locusts, इव like, केदारम् a field, मशकाः mosquitoes, इव like, पर्वतम् a mountain, यथा just as, अमृतघटम् a pot of nectar, दंशाः flies, मकराः crocodiles, इव like, च and, अर्णवम् the ocean,

40020090.author: Translation
40020090.content: Just as locusts swarm a field, mosquitoes a mountain, flies a pot of nectar, and crocodiles the ocean, so too did the arrows approach Hari.

40020091.author: पदार्थः
40020091.content: तथा similarly, रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ताः released from the bows of demons, वज्रानिलमनोजवाः having the speed of lightning, wind, and mind, हरिम् into Hari, विशन्ति स्म entered, शराः arrows, लोकाः worlds, इव like, विपर्यये at the time of dissolution,

40020091.author: Translation
40020091.content: Similarly, arrows released from the bows of demons, possessing the speed of lightning, wind, and mind, entered Hari, just as all beings merge into the supreme at the time of cosmic dissolution.

40020092.author: पदार्थः
40020092.content: स्यन्दनैः with chariots, स्यन्दनगताः those who went in chariots, गजैः with elephants, च and, गजपृष्ठगाः those who went on elephant-backs, अश्वारोहाः horse-riders, तथा similarly, अश्वैः with horses, च and, पादाताः foot-soldiers, च and, अम्बरे in the sky, स्थिताः standing,

40020092.author: Translation
40020092.content: Those who rode in chariots, those on elephant-backs, horse-riders with their horses, and foot-soldiers, all were positioned in the sky.

40020093.author: पदार्थः
40020093.content: राक्षसेन्द्राः demon lords, गिरिनिभाः mountain-like, शरैः with arrows, शक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः with spears, lances, and javelins, निरुछ्वासं breathless, हरिं Hari, चक्रुः made, प्राणायामाः breath control exercises, इव like, द्विजम् a brahmin.

40020093.author: Translation
40020093.content: The mountain-like demon lords, using arrows, spears, lances, and javelins, rendered Hari breathless, just as breath control exercises make a brahmin breathless.

40020094.author: पदार्थः
40020094.content: निशाचरैः by night-wanderers, ताड्यमानो being struck, मीनैरिव like by fish, महोदधिः the great ocean, शार्ङ्गम् the Sharnga bow, आयम्य having drawn, दुर्धर्षो the unconquerable one, राक्षसेभ्यो at the demons, असृजत् released, शरान् arrows.

40020094.author: Translation
40020094.content: Being tormented by the night-wanderers like the great ocean by fish, the unconquerable one drew his Sharnga bow and discharged arrows at the demons.

40020095.author: पदार्थः
40020095.content: शरैः with arrows, पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः fully drawn and released, वज्रवक्त्रैः having thunderbolt-like points, मनोजवैः swift as thought, चिच्छेद cut, विष्णुः Vishnu, निशितैः sharp, शतशो by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands.

40020095.author: Translation
40020095.content: With sharp arrows, fully drawn and released, having thunderbolt-like points and swift as thought, Vishnu cut them down by hundreds and then by thousands.

40020096.author: पदार्थः
40020096.content: विद्राव्य having dispersed, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, वर्षा rain, वायुः wind, इव like, उत्थितम् risen, पाञ्चजन्यं the Panchajanya, महाशङ्खं the great conch, प्रदध्मौ blew, पुरुषोत्तमः the best among men.

40020096.author: Translation
40020096.content: Having dispersed the rain of arrows with his own arrows, just as wind disperses rain, the best among men blew his great conch, Panchajanya.

40020097.author: पदार्थः
40020097.content: सः that, अम्बुजः water-born (conch), हरिणा by Hari, ध्मातः blown, सर्वप्राणेन with all his might, शङ्खराट् the king of conches, ररास roared, भीमनिर्हादः with a terrible roar, त्रैलोक्यं the three worlds, व्यथयन् distressing, इव as if.

40020097.author: Translation
40020097.content: That water-born king of conches, blown by Hari with all his might, roared with a terrible sound, as if terrifying the three worlds.

40020098.author: पदार्थः
40020098.content: शङ्खराजरवः the sound of the king of conches, सः that, अथ then, त्रासयामास terrified, राक्षसान् the Rākṣasas, मृगराजः a lion, इव like, अरण्ये in the forest, समदान् maddened, इव like, कुञ्जरान् elephants.

40020098.author: Translation
40020098.content: Then, the sound of the king of conches terrified the Rākṣasas, just as a lion in the forest frightens maddened elephants.

40020099.author: पदार्थः
40020099.content: न not, शेकुः were able, अश्वाः horses, संस्थातुम् to stand still, विमदाः bereft of ichor/strength, कुञ्जराः elephants, अभवन् became, स्यन्दनेभ्यः from their chariots, च्युताः fallen, वीराः warriors, शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः weakened by the conch's sound.

40020099.author: Translation
40020099.content: The horses were unable to stand still, the elephants lost their ichor and strength, and warriors, weakened by the conch's sound, fell from their chariots.

40020100.author: पदार्थः
40020100.content: शार्ङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ताः released from the Śārṅga bow, वज्रतुल्याननाः having points like a thunderbolt, शराः arrows, विदार्य tearing apart, तानि those, रक्षांसि Rākṣasas, सुपुङ्खाः with good feathers, विविशुः entered, क्षितिम् the earth.

40020100.author: Translation
40020100.content: Arrows released from the Śārṅga bow, with points like thunderbolts, tore through those Rākṣasas and, with their well-feathered shafts, penetrated the earth.

40020101.author: पदार्थः
40020101.content: भिद्यमानाः being pierced, शरैः by arrows, सङ्ख्ये in battle, नारायणकरच्युतैः released from Nārāyaṇa's hand, निपेतू fell, राक्षसाः the Rākṣasas, भूमौ on the ground, शैलाः mountains, वज्रहताः struck by a thunderbolt, इव like.

40020101.author: Translation
40020101.content: Being pierced by arrows released from Nārāyaṇa's hand in battle, the Rākṣasas fell to the ground like mountains struck by a thunderbolt.

40020102.author: पदार्थः
40020102.content: व्रणानि wounds, परगात्रेभ्यः from the bodies of the enemies, विष्णुचक्रकृतानि made by Viṣṇu's discus, वै indeed, असृक् blood, क्षरन्ति flowed, धाराभिः in streams, स्वर्णधाराः streams of gold, इव like, अचलाः mountains.

40020102.author: Translation
40020102.content: From the enemies' bodies, wounds made by Viṣṇu's discus indeed streamed blood in torrents, resembling mountains from which streams of gold flow.

40020103.author: पदार्थः
40020103.content: शङ्खराजरवः the sound of the king of conches, च and, अपि also, शार्ङ्गचापरस्वः the twang of the Śārṅga bow, तथा similarly, राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, रवान् sounds, च and, अपि also, ग्रसते devours, वैष्णवः the sound pertaining to Viṣṇu, रवः sound.

40020103.author: Translation
40020103.content: The sound of Viṣṇu's conch and the twang of his Śārṅga bow completely overpower and swallow the roars of the Rākṣasas.

40020104.author: पदार्थः
40020104.content: तेषाम् their, शिरोधरान् necks, धूतान् severed, शरध्वजधनूंषि arrows, banners, and bows, च and, रथान् chariots, पताकाः flags, तूणीरान् quivers, चिच्छेद cut, सः he, हरिः Hari, शरैः with arrows.

40020104.author: Translation
40020104.content: Hari, with his arrows, severed their necks, and cut down their arrows, banners, bows, chariots, flags, and quivers.

40020105.author: पदार्थः
40020105.content: सूर्यात् from the sun, इव as if, कराः rays, घोराः terrible, ऊर्मयः waves, सागरात् from the ocean, इव as if, पर्वतात् from mountains, इव as if, नागेन्द्राः great elephants, धारौघाः torrents of rain, इव as if, च and, अम्बुदात् from a cloud.

40020105.author: Translation
40020105.content: Just as terrible rays emanate from the sun, waves from the ocean, great elephants from mountains, and torrents of rain from a cloud, so too did arrows emerge.

40020106.author: पदार्थः
40020106.content: तथा similarly, शार्ङ्गविनिर्मुक्ताः released from the Śārṅga bow, शराः arrows, नारायणेरिताः propelled by Nārāyaṇa, निर्धावन्ति rushed forth, इषवः arrows, तूर्णं swiftly, शतशः by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands.

40020106.author: Translation
40020106.content: Similarly, arrows released from the Śārṅga bow and propelled by Nārāyaṇa rushed forth swiftly by hundreds and thousands.

40020107.author: पदार्थः
40020107.content: शरभेण by a Śarabha, यथा as, सिंहाः lions, सिंहेन by a lion, द्विरदाः elephants, यथा as, द्विरदेन by an elephant, यथा as, व्याघ्राः tigers, व्याघ्रेण by a tiger, द्वीपिनः leopards, यथा as.

40020107.author: Translation
40020107.content: Just as lions are overcome by a Śarabha, elephants by a lion, tigers by an elephant, and leopards by a tiger, so too were the Rākṣasas overwhelmed.

40020108.author: पदार्थः
40020108.content: द्वीपिनेन by a leopard, इव as if, यथा just as, श्वानः dogs, शुना by a dog, मार्जारकाः cats, यथा just as, मार्जारेण by a cat, यथा just as, सर्पाः snakes, सर्पेण by a snake, च and, यथा just as, आखवः mice.

40020108.author: Translation
40020108.content: Just as dogs are afraid of a leopard, cats of a dog, snakes of a cat, and mice of a snake, so too were the rakshasas.

40020109.author: पदार्थः
40020109.content: तथा similarly, ते those, राक्षसाः rakshasas, सर्वे all, विष्णुना by Vishnu, प्रभविष्णुना by the all-powerful, द्रवन्ति flee, द्राविताः put to flight, च and, अन्ये others, शायिताः laid down, च and, महीतले on the ground.

40020109.author: Translation
40020109.content: Similarly, all those rakshasas fled from the all-powerful Vishnu, while others were put to flight or laid dead on the ground.

40020110.author: पदार्थः
40020110.content: राक्षसानाम् of rakshasas, सहस्राणि thousands, निहत्य having killed, मधुसूदनः Madhusudana, वारिजम् the conch, पूरयामास he blew, तोयदम् a cloud, सुरराट् the king of gods, इव as if.

40020110.author: Translation
40020110.content: Having slain thousands of rakshasas, Madhusudana blew his conch, just as the king of gods (Indra) causes a cloud to thunder.

40020111.author: पदार्थः
40020111.content: नारायणशरत्रस्तम् terrified by Narayana's arrows, शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम् greatly bewildered by the sound of the conch, ययौ went, लङ्काम् to Lanka, अभिमुखम् facing towards, प्रभग्नम् routed, राक्षसम् rakshasa, बलम् army.

40020111.author: Translation
40020111.content: The routed rakshasa army, terrified by Narayana's arrows and greatly bewildered by the sound of his conch, fled towards Lanka.

40020112.author: पदार्थः
40020112.content: प्रभग्ने when routed, राक्षसबले the rakshasa army, नारायणशराहते struck by Narayana's arrows, सुमाली Sumali, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, निववार he obstructed, रणे in battle, हरिम् Hari.

40020112.author: Translation
40020112.content: When the rakshasa army was routed and struck by Narayana's arrows, Sumali, in battle, obstructed Hari with a shower of arrows.

40020113.author: पदार्थः
40020113.content: सः he, तु indeed, तम् him, छादयामास covered, नीहारः mist, इव like, भास्करम् the sun. राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, सत्त्वसम्पन्नाः endowed with strength, पुनः again, धैर्यम् courage, समादधुः regained.

40020113.author: Translation
40020113.content: He covered him like mist covers the sun, and the Rakshasas, filled with courage, regained their composure.

40020114.author: पदार्थः
40020114.content: अथ then, सः he, अभ्यपतत् rushed towards, रोषात् from anger, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, बलदर्पितः proud of his strength. महानादम् a great roar, प्रकुर्वाणः making, राक्षसान् the Rakshasas, जीवयन् enlivening, इव as if.

40020114.author: Translation
40020114.content: Then, that Rakshasa, proud of his strength, rushed forward in anger, making a great roar as if to revive the other Rakshasas.

40020115.author: पदार्थः
40020115.content: उत्क्षिप्य lifting up, लम्बाभरणम् his long ornaments, धुन्वन् shaking, करम् his trunk, इव like, द्विपः an elephant. ररास roared, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, हर्षात् from joy, सतडित् with lightning, तोयदः a cloud, यथा just as.

40020115.author: Translation
40020115.content: Lifting his long ornaments and shaking them like an elephant shakes its trunk, the Rakshasa roared with joy, just like a thunderous cloud.

40020116.author: पदार्थः
40020116.content: सुमालेः of Sumali, नर्दतः roaring, तस्य his, शिरः head, ज्वलितकुण्डलम् with shining earrings. चिच्छेद cut off, यन्तुः of the charioteer, अश्वाः horses, च and, भ्रान्ताः bewildered, तस्य his, तु indeed, रक्षसः of the Rakshasa.

40020116.author: Translation
40020116.content: (He) cut off the head of the roaring Sumali, which was adorned with shining earrings, and the horses of that Rakshasa's charioteer became bewildered.

40020117.author: पदार्थः
40020117.content: तैः by those, अश्वैः horses, भ्रान्तैः bewildered, भ्राम्यते was whirled around, सुमाली Sumali, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rakshasas. इन्द्रियाश्वैः by the horses of senses, परिभ्रान्तैः bewildered, धृतिहीनः devoid of steadfastness, यथा just as, नरः a man.

40020117.author: Translation
40020117.content: Sumali, the lord of Rakshasas, was whirled around by those bewildered horses, just as a man devoid of steadfastness is bewildered by the horses of his senses.

40020118.author: पदार्थः
40020118.content: ततः then, विष्णुम् Vishnu, महाबाहुम् the mighty-armed, प्रपतन्तम् falling down, रणाजिरे in the battlefield, हृते when taken away, सुमालेः by Sumali, अश्वैः by horses, च and, रथे the chariot, विष्णुरथम् Vishnu's chariot, प्रति towards

40020118.author: Translation
40020118.content: Then, as Vishnu's chariot was carried away by Sumali's horses, the mighty-armed Vishnu was seen falling down in the battlefield.

40020119.author: पदार्थः
40020119.content: माली Mali, च and, अभ्यद्रवत् rushed towards, युक्तः ready, प्रगृह्य holding, सशरम् with arrows, धनुः bow, मालेः from Mali's, धनुः bow, च्युताः released, बाणाः arrows, कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः adorned with gold, विविशुः entered, हरिम् Vishnu, आसाद्य reaching, क्रौञ्चम् the Krauncha mountain, पत्ररथाः birds, इव like

40020119.author: Translation
40020119.content: Mali, ready and holding his bow with arrows, rushed towards Vishnu, and the gold-adorned arrows released from his bow pierced Vishnu, just as birds enter the Krauncha mountain.

40020120.author: पदार्थः
40020120.content: अर्द्यमानः being tormented, शरैः by arrows, सः he (Vishnu), अथ then, मालिमुक्तैः released by Mali, सहस्रशः by thousands, चुक्षुभे न did not become agitated, रणे in battle, विष्णुः Vishnu, जितेन्द्रियः one who has controlled his senses, इव like, अधिभिः by mental anxieties

40020120.author: Translation
40020120.content: Though tormented by thousands of arrows released by Mali, Vishnu remained unagitated in battle, like a person who has controlled his senses is unaffected by mental anxieties.

40020121.author: पदार्थः
40020121.content: अथ then, मौर्वीस्वनम् the twang of the bowstring, कृत्वा making, भगवान् the divine one, भूतभावनः the creator of beings, मालिनम् Mali, प्रति towards, बाणौघान् showers of arrows, ससर्ज released, अरिनिषूदनः the destroyer of enemies

40020121.author: Translation
40020121.content: Then, the divine creator of beings and destroyer of enemies, making the twang of his bowstring, released showers of arrows towards Mali.

40020122.author: पदार्थः
40020122.content: ते those, मालिदेहम् Mali's body, आसाद्य reaching, वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः having the brilliance of thunderbolt and lightning, शराः arrows, पिबन्ति drank, रुधिरम् blood, तस्य his, नागाः serpents, इव like, सुधारसम् nectar

40020122.author: Translation
40020122.content: Those arrows, shining like thunderbolts and lightning, reached Mali's body and drank his blood as if serpents were drinking nectar.

40020123.author: पदार्थः
40020123.content: मालिनं Mali, विमुखं facing away, कृत्वा having made, शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः the one holding conch, discus, and mace, मालिमौलिं Mali's crown, ध्वजं banner, चापं bow, वाजिनः horses, च and, अपि also, अपातयत् struck down.

40020123.author: Translation
40020123.content: The wielder of the conch, discus, and mace turned Mali away and then struck down Mali's crown, banner, bow, and horses.

40020124.author: पदार्थः
40020124.content: विरथः chariot-less, तु but, गदां mace, गृह्य having taken, माली Mali, नक्तञ्चरोत्तमः the best among night-wanderers, आपुप्लुवे sprang, गदापाणिः mace-in-hand, गिरि mountain, अग्रात् from the peak, इव like, केसरी a lion.

40020124.author: Translation
40020124.content: But Mali, the foremost among night-roaming demons, having lost his chariot, took up his mace and, mace in hand, sprang forward like a lion from a mountain peak.

40020125.author: पदार्थः
40020125.content: गदया with the mace, गरुडेशानं the lord of Garuda, ईशानं Shiva, इव like, च and, अन्तकः Yama, ललाटदेशे on the forehead region, अभ्यहनत् struck, वज्रेण with the thunderbolt, इन्द्रः Indra, यथा as, अचलम् a mountain.

40020125.author: Translation
40020125.content: With his mace, Mali struck the lord of Garuda on the forehead, just as Yama strikes Shiva, or as Indra strikes a mountain with his thunderbolt.

40020126.author: पदार्थः
40020126.content: गदया by the mace, अभिहतः struck, तेन by him, मालिना by Mali, गरुडः Garuda, भृशम् severely, रणात् from the battle, पराङ्मुखं facing away, देवं the god, कृतवान् made, वेदनातुरः distressed by pain.

40020126.author: Translation
40020126.content: Severely struck by Mali's mace, Garuda, distressed by the pain, caused the god (Vishnu) to turn away from the battle.

40020127.author: पदार्थः
40020127.content: पराङ्मुखे facing away, कृते having been made, देवे the god, मालिना by Mali, गरुडेन by Garuda, वै indeed, उदतिष्ठत् arose, महान् great, शब्दः sound, रक्षसां of the demons, अभिनर्दताम् roaring.

40020127.author: Translation
40020127.content: When the god was indeed made to turn away by Mali (through Garuda), a great roaring sound arose from the exultant demons.

40020128.author: पदार्थः
40020128.content: रक्षसां of the Rākṣasas, रवतां roaring, रावं sound, श्रुत्वा having heard, हरिहयानुजः the younger brother of Harihaya (Indra, i.e., Vishnu).

40020128.author: Translation
40020128.content: Having heard the roaring sound of the Rākṣasas, Vishnu, the younger brother of Indra, reacted.

40020129.author: पदार्थः
40020129.content: तिर्यगास्थाय having stood obliquely, सङ्क्रुद्धः greatly enraged, पक्षीशे on the lord of birds (Garuda), भगवान् the divine, हरिः Hari (Vishnu), पराङ्मुखो ऽपि even though facing away, उत्ससर्ज released, मालेः at Māli, चक्रं the discus, जिघांसया with the desire to kill.

40020129.author: Translation
40020129.content: The divine Hari, greatly enraged, stood sideways on Garuda and, even while facing away, released his discus at Māli with the intention of killing him.

40020130.author: पदार्थः
40020130.content: तत् that, सूर्यमण्डलाभासं resembling the orb of the sun, स्वभासा with its own radiance, भासयन् illuminating, नभः the sky, कालचक्रनिभं resembling the wheel of time, चक्रं discus, मालेः of Māli, शीर्षम् head, अपातयत् cut off.

40020130.author: Translation
40020130.content: That discus, resembling the sun's orb and illuminating the sky with its own brilliance, and appearing like the wheel of time, severed Māli's head.

40020131.author: पदार्थः
40020131.content: तत् that, शिरो head, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the king of Rākṣasas, चक्रोत्कृत्तं severed by the discus, बिभीषणम् terrifying, पपात fell, रुधिरोद्गारि gushing blood, पुरा formerly, राहुशिरो Rāhu's head, यथा just as.

40020131.author: Translation
40020131.content: That terrifying head of the king of Rākṣasas, severed by the discus and gushing blood, fell just as Rāhu's head had fallen in ancient times.

40020132.author: पदार्थः
40020132.content: ततः then, सुरैः by the gods, संसहृष्टैः greatly delighted, सर्वप्राणसमीरितः uttered with all their might, सिंहनादरवः a lion's roar (a mighty shout), उन्मुक्तः released, साधु देव "Well done, O God!", इतिवादिभिः those who said thus.

40020132.author: Translation
40020132.content: Then, the greatly delighted gods, exclaiming "Well done, O God!", uttered a mighty roar with all their might.

40020133.author: पदार्थः
40020133.content: मालिनं Malina, निहतं slain, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सुमाली Sumali, माल्यवानपि and Malyavan also, सबलौ with their forces, शोकसन्तप्तौ tormented by grief, लङ्कामेव to Lanka itself, प्रधावितौ they fled

40020133.author: Translation
40020133.content: Seeing Malina slain, Sumali and Malyavan, along with their armies, were overcome with grief and fled back to Lanka.

40020134.author: पदार्थः
40020134.content: गरुडस्तु but Garuda, समाश्वस्तः having recovered, सन्निवृत्य having returned, यथा as, पुरा before, राक्षसान् the Rakshasas, द्रावयामास he made to flee, पक्षवातेन by the wind from his wings, कोपितः enraged

40020134.author: Translation
40020134.content: Garuda, having recovered and returned as before, angrily chased away the Rakshasas with the powerful wind generated by his wings.

40020135.author: पदार्थः
40020135.content: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलाः whose lotus-like faces were severed by the discus, गदासञ्चूर्णितोरसः whose chests were crushed by maces, लाङ्गलग्लपितग्रीवाः whose necks were destroyed by ploughs, मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकाः whose heads were shattered by pestles

40020135.author: Translation
40020135.content: The Rakshasas had their lotus-like faces severed by the discus, their chests crushed by maces, their necks destroyed by ploughs, and their heads shattered by pestles.

40020136.author: पदार्थः
40020136.content: केचित् some, चैव and indeed, असिना by swords, छिन्नाः cut, तथान्ये similarly others, शरपीडिताः tormented by arrows, निपेतुरम्बरात् fell from the sky, तूर्णं quickly, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, सागराम्भसि into the ocean's waters

40020136.author: Translation
40020136.content: Some Rakshasas were cut down by swords, others were wounded by arrows, and all of them swiftly fell from the sky into the ocean's waters.

40020137.author: पदार्थः
40020137.content: नारायणो Narayana, बाणवराशनीभिः with excellent arrows like thunderbolts, विदारयामास tore apart, धनुर्विमुक्तैः released from his bow, नक्तञ्चरान् the night-wanderers (Rakshasas), मुक्तविधूतकेशान् whose hair was loose and disheveled, यथा just as, अशनीभिः by thunderbolts, सतडिन्महाभ्राः great clouds with lightning

40020137.author: Translation
40020137.content: Narayana, with excellent arrows released from his bow like thunderbolts, tore apart the night-wandering Rakshasas whose hair was loose and disheveled, just as thunderbolts tear apart great clouds accompanied by lightning.

40020138.author: पदार्थः
40020138.content: भिन्नातपत्रं with broken umbrellas, पतमानमस्त्रं with falling weapons, शरैः by arrows, अपध्वस्तविनीतवेषम् with proper attire destroyed, विनिस्सृतान्त्रं with intestines gushing out, भयलोलनेत्रं with eyes rolling in fear, बलं the army, तत् that, उन्मत्ततरं more maddened, बभूव became

40020138.author: Translation
40020138.content: The army became utterly frenzied, with their royal canopies shattered, weapons dropping, proper attire torn by arrows, intestines spilling out, and eyes wide with terror.

40020139.author: पदार्थः
40020139.content: सिंहार्दितानाम् of those tormented by a lion, इव like, कुञ्जराणां of elephants, निशाचराणां of night-rovers (Rakshasas), सह with, कुञ्जराणाम् of elephants, रवाः roars/cries, च and, वेगाः speeds/rushes, च and, समं together/simultaneously, बभूवुः became/occurred, पुराणसिंहेन by the ancient lion, विमर्दितानाम् of those crushed

40020139.author: Translation
40020139.content: The roars and frantic movements of the Rakshasas and their elephants, tormented by the ancient lion, were like those of elephants distressed by a lion.

40020140.author: पदार्थः
40020140.content: ते they, वार्यमाणाः being obstructed/repelled, हरिबाणजालैः by the showers of arrows from the Vanaras, सबाणजालानि their own showers of arrows, समुत्सृजन्तः abandoning/throwing away, धावन्ति run, नक्तञ्चरकालमेघाः the Rakshasas, like dark clouds, वायुप्रभिन्नाः scattered by the wind, इव like, कालमेघाः dark clouds

40020140.author: Translation
40020140.content: Those Rakshasas, like dark clouds, were repelled by the showers of arrows from the Vanaras, and abandoning their own arrows, they fled like storm clouds scattered by the wind.

40020141.author: पदार्थः
40020141.content: चक्रपहारैः by blows of discus, विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः with severed heads, सञ्चूर्णिताङ्गाः with crushed limbs, च and, गदाप्रहारैः by blows of mace, अभिप्रहारैः by various attacks, द्विविधाः in two ways/halves, विभिन्नाः split/torn apart, पतन्ति fall, शैलाः mountains, इव like, राक्षसेन्द्राः Rakshasa lords/chiefs

40020141.author: Translation
40020141.content: The chief Rakshasas, with their heads severed by discus blows, limbs crushed by mace blows, and bodies split in two by various attacks, fell like mountains.

40020142.author: पदार्थः
40020142.content: विलम्बमानैः hanging down, मणिहारकुण्डलैः with jewel necklaces and earrings, निशाचरैः by the night-rovers (Rakshasas), नीलबलाहकोपमैः resembling blue clouds, निपात्यमानैः being struck down/falling, ददृशे was seen, निरन्तरं continuously/without gap, निपात्यमानैः being struck down/falling, इव like, नीलपर्वतैः by blue mountains

40020142.author: Translation
40020142.content: The falling Rakshasas, who resembled dark blue clouds and wore dangling jewel necklaces and earrings, were continuously seen falling like blue mountains being struck down. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः ।। 7 ।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
